first_operational.notes: T1 NSFNET service entered production in 1988; exact first operational date per NSS site should be recorded separately.

withdrawn.notes: T1 NSS equipment was dismantled after traffic migrated to the T3 backbone; site-specific removal dates vary.

physical.medium: T1 carrier circuits on the backbone side; dual IBM Token Ring internal fabrics; Ethernet client attachment
physical.line_service: 1.544 Mbit/s T1 with multiple logical links possible at sub-T1 through full-T1 rates
physical.clocking: Carrier/T1 and internal-interface clocking details pending hardware records
physical.signaling: T1 through DSU/CSU and WACS; exact framing/line coding pending site records
interfaces: T1 via DSU/CSU and Wide-Area Communications Subsystem

hardware.processor: Nine IBM RT systems processors in the generic NSS design; exact RT model/submodel unresolved
hardware.memory: Role- and site-specific RAM configuration unresolved
hardware.storage: Role- and site-specific disk/boot-media configuration unresolved
boards_or_modules: 4 × IBM RT Packet Switching Processor roles shown in Merit Figure 14
1 × IBM RT External Packet Switching Processor
3 × backup IBM RT systems omitted from Merit Figure 14
1 × IBM PS/2 Model 80 NetView PC LAN Manager
hardware.rack_or_enclosure: Multiple racks; SESQUINET shipment recollection says three racks, but generic rack layout remains unresolved

software.operating_system: Modified 4.3BSD / Berkeley UNIX on IBM RT processors
software.version_or_revision: 1988 T1 NSFNET generation; release-level build identifiers pending

addressing: RFC 1074 documents IP information encoded into NSAP-like structures for the adapted IS-IS implementation; attached networks exchanged reachability through EGP.
routing_or_forwarding: The NSS was treated as one routing entity. RCP/PSP architecture separated routing control from packet switching; SPF topology calculation used an adapted ANSI IS-IS design and EGP/policy controls governed attached networks.
error_control: Link- and device-specific mechanisms existed below IP; exact T1/WACS and internal Token Ring behavior requires hardware/software recovery.
flow_or_congestion_control: Queueing/forwarding behavior is known to have existed in the packet processors but exact queue structures, drop policy and tuning are unresolved.

operations.monitoring: Remote production monitoring through the Merit Network Operations Center; network status, statistics and management data were displayed/collected centrally.
operations.diagnostics: NOC, IBM, MCI and site personnel used documented escalation and troubleshooting procedures; exact commands/test interfaces pending Site Manual recovery.
operations.remote_management: Management paths linked site NSS systems to the Ann Arbor operational environment; protocol/software details remain to be reconstructed.
operations.failure_behavior: Redundancy was a design goal; three backup RTs were available in the generic architecture, but failover state machine and automation level are unresolved.
operations.operator_interface: Site consoles plus PS/2 management systems and Ann Arbor NOC displays; exact screens/commands pending preservation.

economics.payer_or_funder: NSF-funded backbone partnership with Merit, IBM, MCI and state/academic participants

geography: Thirteen T1-era NSFNET backbone sites in the continental United States

survival.provenance_notes: A December 1992 NANOG message offered approximately 4–6 former NSS IBM RT workstations per site to hosting regional networks after dismantling. Recipient/serial-number provenance remains to be recovered.
